title: Anchor enrichment: exclude high-frequency import patterns
description:
## Problem

Auto-enrichment on `sutra_remember` generates import_pattern anchors for all imports in the anchored file. Infrastructure crates like `parking_lot`, `serde`, and `schemars` appear in most source files, so lessons anchored to them surface everywhere — defeating the purpose of contextual surfacing.

Current state: `parking_lot::*` is an anchor on all 5 verified lessons. Any file importing parking_lot (8 files) sees all 5 lessons regardless of relevance. The MCP server lesson surfaces when reading `Db::replace_file_data` solely because both files import parking_lot.

## What to build

During anchor enrichment in `sutra_remember`, filter out import_pattern anchors whose import appears in more than N files in the workspace (suggested threshold: files importing the crate > 30% of total source files, or a hard cap like >5 files). Alternatively, maintain a denylist of infrastructure crates (`parking_lot`, `serde`, `schemars`, `std::*`).

Also retroactively clean the existing anchors — delete import_pattern anchors for the denied crates from the 5 migrated lessons.

## Files

- `src/lessons.rs` — the `store_with_enrichment` or equivalent method that generates import_pattern anchors
- `~/.sutra/lessons.db` — one-time cleanup of existing noisy anchors
execution_record: Three filters added to enrichment: (1) import_root skips `pub use` re-exports, (2) import_pattern anchors skipped when the root crate appears in >5 workspace files (via new Db::import_root_file_counts), (3) directory anchors skipped when top-level (no `/` separator). Retroactively cleaned 21 noisy import_pattern anchors and 3 top-level directory anchors from existing lessons. Surfacing precision: Db::replace_file_data 4→2 lessons, SutraServer 4→2, DdEngine::query_violations 3→1."

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Adversarial review — verdict: needs-attention

**Finding 1 [high]: Root frequency counts inflated — not counting distinct files per root**
`import_root_file_counts()` groups by full `imported_path`, counts distinct files per exact path, then sums after extracting the root. A file importing both `rusqlite::params` and `rusqlite::Connection` contributes 2 to `rusqlite`'s count, even though the method promises distinct files per root. With a hard cap of 5, three files importing two items from the same crate hit frequency 6 and the crate anchor is suppressed — false positive.
Recommendation: Count distinct `(root, file_id)` pairs instead. Share the root-extraction helper with enrichment, collect `HashSet<i64>` per root from `SELECT file_id, imported_path FROM imports`, then convert set lengths.

**Finding 2 [high]: Existing noisy import anchors not cleaned up**
The new logic only skips adding new `ImportPattern` anchors during `sutra_remember`; it does not remove or ignore previously stored anchors. The task description says verified lessons already have anchors like `parking_lot::*`, and those persisted anchors still match during lesson surfacing. Creation-time filter alone leaves the user-visible pollution in place for the exact lessons that motivated the task.
Recommendation: Add explicit cleanup or query-time suppression for existing high-frequency `import_pattern` anchors.

messages.text:
Fixed both codex review findings in f2dd60d:
1. import_root_file_counts now collects HashSet<i64> per root — each file counted once regardless of how many symbols it imports from that crate.
2. Added LessonsDb::prune_high_freq_import_anchors — deletes persisted import_pattern anchors for roots exceeding the cap. Called on every sutra_remember invocation, so existing noisy anchors (parking_lot::*, serde::*, etc.) are cleaned up on next use.
